ch29.b.d.wire: Shape of the current-carrying wire (drag the field point $P$)
ch29.b.d.n: Number of current elements $d\vec l$ the wire is cut into
ch29.b.goal.sum: Biot-Savart law: the field of the whole wire is the sum of the $d\vec B$ of each current element $I\,d\vec l$
ch29.b.goal.dir: $d\vec B$ is perpendicular to both $d\vec l$ and $\vec r$. With the wire and the field point in one plane, $d\vec B$ is perpendicular to the page (⊙ out, ⊗ in)
ch29.b.obs.play: Play: elements are added one by one. The plots show each element's $dB$ and the running sum $B$
ch29.b.obs.far: Straight wire: elements far from the field point contribute little ($1/r^2$ and $\sin\theta$); the nearby ones make most of the sum
ch29.b.obs.r: Drag $P$ away from the wire: $B$ falls as $1/d$; compare with the dashed reference $\mu_0 I/2\pi d$
ch29.b.obs.loop: Centre of the loop: every element gives the same $dB$ in the same direction, summing to $\mu_0 I/2R$
ch29.b.obs.inside: Inside the loop the field is ⊙; outside, the nearby elements dominate and it is ⊗
ch29.b.obs.n: More elements give nearly the same sum (smaller elements are more accurate)
ch29.b.as.units: Current $I = 10$ A, lengths in m, field in μT
ch29.b.as.plane: The wire and the field point lie in one plane (the page)
ch29.b.as.mid: Each element's contribution is evaluated at its midpoint (midpoint rule)
ch29.b.as.ref: The straight wire is 2.2 m long; the dashed reference $\mu_0 I/2\pi d$ is the value for an infinitely long wire. Loop radius $R = 0.45$ m
ch29.a.d.preset: Starting arrangement of the wires (drag to move; the tray at the lower left adds and removes)
ch29.a.d.shape: Shape of the closed path (drag the centre point to move it, the points on the edge to resize or reshape it)
ch29.a.d.view: Draw the field as field lines or grid arrows, or hide it
ch29.a.goal.law: Ampère's law: $\oint \vec B\cdot d\vec l$ around a closed path equals $\mu_0$ times the current through it, whatever the shape
ch29.a.goal.out: Currents outside the path change $\vec B$ on it but add nothing to the circulation
ch29.a.obs.single: Single wire: the field lines are circles around the wire, $B \propto 1/r$
ch29.a.obs.pair: Opposite pair: a loop around both has $I_\text{enc} = 0$, so $\oint \vec B\cdot d\vec l = 0$ although $\vec B$ on the path is not zero
ch29.a.obs.solenoid: Solenoid section: strong, nearly uniform field inside, weak field outside. A loop around the top row gives the number of wires enclosed × $\mu_0 I$
ch29.a.obs.arrows: Arrows on the path: the tangential component $B_t$, vermilion along the path (counter-clockwise), blue against it
ch29.a.obs.shape: Stretching or reshaping the loop leaves the value unchanged as long as it encloses the same current
ch29.a.obs.tray: Tray at the lower left: add or remove ⊙ (1 A out of the page) and ⊗ (1 A into the page)
ch29.a.as.2d: Cross-sections of infinitely long straight wires perpendicular to the page, $B = \mu_0 I/2\pi r$; the solenoid section has finite length, so the field outside is not exactly zero
ch29.a.as.units: 1 A per wire, lengths in m, $\oint \vec B\cdot d\vec l$ in μT·m
ch29.a.as.sign: The path runs counter-clockwise; by the right-hand rule a ⊙ current counts as positive
ch29.a.as.num: $\oint \vec B\cdot d\vec l$ is a numerical integral along the path. Wires are kept at least 3.5 cm from the path
